summary: Tenant geo-split migration: intermittent egress to wrong region causing p95 latency and TLS retries
description: Issue summary: After initiating a tenant geo-split migration (ClearSight Analytics) to move production traffic from us-west to eu-west, a subset of inference requests continued to egress via us-west for ~10-30s windows, causing p95 latency to jump from ~120ms to ~850ms and sporadic TLS renegotiation errors. Impact: Customer reports degraded latency for EU-based users and elevated error rate (502/524) during cutover. Environment: Production, dedicated tenant on Redwood Dedicated using strict residency=true and model redwood-gpt-large-v2 pinned. Expected: All traffic for tenant should egress in eu-west after migration cutover. Observed: Intermittent cross-region egress and TLS handshake retries correlated with our control-plane maintenance window and edge cert rotation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer triggered geo-split migration using console 'Start region migration' for tenant ID T-7391
2) Control-plane rollout initiated pin refresh and edge coordinator scheduled edge cert rotation
3) Observe traffic during cutover windows using customer's p95 latency dashboards and our tokens/egress logs
logs: 2026-03-10T02:14:31Z EDGE-LB: selector=eu-west-1 -> routed to us-west-2 (fallback) reason=pin-refresh-expired ttl_remaining=0
2026-03-10T02:14:34Z TLS: handshake error: remote_renegotiate during connection to 44.210.11.72:443, retry_count=2
2026-03-10T02:14:35Z CONTROL-PLANE: residency-binding refresh start for tenant=T-7391, change_set=geo-split, rollout_id=rl-2026-03-10-02
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: residency pin-expiry and edge healthcheck flapping during cert rotation caused routing fallback to nearest capacity (us-west-2) despite strict residency flag set.
Checked control-plane logs: refresh requests for tenant T-7391 completed, but there is a 12s delay between control-plane commit and edge-lb binding reconciliation during the rolling upgrade.

Edge LB telemetry shows NAT session affinity causing existing upstream TCP sessions to persist to us-west-2 while new sessions prefer eu-west-1; combined with cert reissuance we saw TLS renegotiation and short-lived 5xx bursts.

Found a codepath in edge-lb that clears residency binding when healthcheck returns soft-fail during certificate replacement; this allowed fallback routing even though strict residency should block egress to non-resident regions.
Reproduced in staging with smaller window by simulating cert rotation while forcing healthcheck timeout; observed identical egress behavior and p95 jump.
comments: 2026-03-10T03:00Z - Aisha Patel: Customer reported initial spike at 02:14 UTC. Attached their p95 chart and sample request IDs.
2026-03-10T04:20Z - Marco Ruiz: Correlated with our scheduled edge cert rotation at 02:12-02:18 UTC. Creating follow-up with edge-lb team to validate healthcheck behavior.
2026-03-11T09:15Z - Priya Shah (SRE): Verified staging repro. Raising severity to Sev1 due to customer P1 impact. Patch proposed to add grace window for residency binding during edge maintenance.
2026-03-12T13:30Z - Marco Ruiz: Patch merged to edge-lb (PR 4872) that prevents residency binding clear on soft-fail during cert rotation. Deployed to canary clusters in eu-west-1 and us-west-2.
2026-03-12T18:45Z - Aisha Patel: Customer validated with synthetic traffic and reports stable p95 ~130ms post-patch. Still monitoring for two full maintenance cycles.
resolution: Workaround/Fix: Deployed edge-lb patch that preserves residency binding during certificate replacement and extends pin-refresh grace window by 30s. Adjusted control-plane requeue to shorten reconciliation lag during rollouts. Customer validation: ClearSight ran two synthetic cutovers — no cross-region egress observed and p95 returned to baseline. Follow-ups: 1) Add metric 'residency_binding_reconcile_lag' and alert for >5s, 2) Update geo-split runbook to pause cert rotations during tenant cutovers unless zero-downtime mode enabled, 3) Postmortem scheduled with edge-lb/infra teams (link in related_confluence_pages).
